title: Refit a popped-out sprung bed slat: seat one end in its holder, bow the slat to drop the other cap under its lip
instruction: Refit the loose bed slat in the empty pair of holders between the two fitted slats, crown up, both end caps seated under the holders' lips, then let go.
context: Sprung (bowed) beech slats in a bed base sit in plastic holders on the side rails, each end cap tucked under a small lip. Slats pop out when a child jumps on the bed or the frame flexes, and putting one back is a common chore: push one end into its holder, bow the slat up so it is short enough to drop the second cap inside the other lip, then let it spring back to length so both caps go home. A slat left resting on top of the holders pops out again under the mattress and someone falls through; a slat bent too far cracks.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), arm bases at y +-30.5. Bed-frame section, loose, 6 kg (estimate): two pine side rails (sRGB 219, 181, 128) 37 x 6.4 x 4.5 cm, x 25.5 to 62.5, inner faces at y +-32.7, outer at y +-39.1, standing on the bench. On each rail three black plastic slat holders (15, 15, 18) at x 30, 41 and 52: a pocket 64 mm wide whose floor is the rail top (4.5 cm above the bench), closed at its outer end by an end wall 18 mm tall with its inner face at y +-37.7 (the two walls of a pair 754.3 mm apart), open at the top and at its inner end 50 mm in from the wall; the end wall's top carries a retaining lip reaching 4 mm in from the wall, its underside 16 mm above the floor; the side walls are vertical to 12 mm and then lean out at 45 deg to 18 mm. The holders at x 30 and x 52 hold fitted slats (loose, 0.25 kg each); the pair at x 41 is empty. Slat (each one): sprung lacquered beech (204, 153, 102), 53 x 8 mm, 755 mm long over its two grey plastic end caps (115, 115, 120; 45 mm long, 58 x 13 mm), bowed 20 mm crown up at rest (end slope 4.7 deg), 0.25 kg; its end-face centres are 753.6 mm apart at rest and the caps' leaning end faces span 754.6 mm over their top edges, so it sits lightly sprung between the end walls and can only be laid in with one end under its lip; the second cap clears its lip with the slat bowed to about 50 mm, 7 mm shorter (about 20 N of lift near a third of its length, estimated). The loose slat lies crown up on its caps on the bench in front of the frame, centred at x 19.5, y 0, along y (seeded: +-1 cm in x, +-2 cm in y, +-4 deg about the vertical).
scoring: Score 0 if at any point: the slat falls off the bench (mid-span more than 5 cm below the bench top); the slat is over-bent (mid-span more than 75 mm above the straight line between its end-face centres, or any of its four hinges bent more than 0.20 rad past its rest angle); a fitted slat moves more than 10 mm; the bed frame moves more than 20 mm. Otherwise, at the end, in the frame's coordinates and only with the caps at opposite holders of the empty pair: a cap is in its holder when its end-face centre is within the 64 mm pocket width and within 27.5 mm of the end wall (at most 1 mm past it), the whole end face below the lip's underside and no more than 2 mm below the floor; seated when also its end-face centre is within 2 mm of the end wall (under the 4 mm lip) and its outer bottom edge within 3 mm of the floor. 1.0 (success): 0.75 held for 1 s with both grippers' centre points at least 5 cm from the slat (the lines from its end-face centres to mid-span) and the slat moving less than 2 mm over that second. 0.75: both caps seated and the slat crown up, mid-span 10 to 40 mm above the line between its end-face centres. 0.5: one cap seated, the other in its holder (seated counts as in). 0.25: one cap seated. Otherwise 0, including doing nothing and laying the slat flat on top of the holders.
reset_notes: Lift the slat out (bow it to free one cap from under its lip) and lay it crown up on its caps on the bench in front of the frame, centred at x 19.5 cm on y 0 along y (the seed sets its offset and angle). Put the frame back with its holders at x 30, 41 and 52 cm, the two fitted slats seated in the outer pairs.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. Slat: five rigid segments on four sprung hinges (25 N m/rad, 8x less stiff than solid beech so YAM's grip can bow it); caps, holders and lead-ins are boxes; caps seat by contact only, no latch. Frame and fitted slats are loose rigid bodies; masses estimated. Crack limits estimated from beech strain. Sim fingers are driven separately, so a held part slides to one finger stop; the demo reads both finger joints.
scores: scripted demo: 1.0 on seeds 0-7, one seed per process (success at steps 1748-1888); do nothing, random joints, random reaches, naive lay-flat: 0.0; Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps, seed 0)
